experiences.title: Forge — Evidence-Aware Coding Agent Workbench
bullets: Kept tool effects auditable: each piece of code evidence carries a source digest and line ranges, every tool action registers a unique action_id in the PostgreSQL ledger before execution, and an unknown outcome stays unknown instead of being automatically redone.

Replayed candidate patches in an independent clean working directory and ran the specified validators, with sandbox execution capped at 2 CPU/2 GiB, a 60 s deadline and no external network; leases renew every 1 s and expire after 3 s.

Moved telemetry off the async control path into two independent bounded SDK queues (64 entries each) with local-record and OTLP fault isolation; in the limited-latency experiment (six paired runs of 24 single-span exports against a fixed 45 ms collector delay) the 10 ms timer measured median per-run p95 event-loop lag of 0.347 ms versus 51.2 ms for the simulated baseline, with 24 local records and 24 OTLP completions per run including drain.

Ran a separate blocking experiment: with the first export held and 200 more spans sent, the 201 total split into 1 in-flight, 64 queued and 136 dropped; the lease still renewed five times during the 5 s block, cancellation reached Docker exit in 0.2 s, and after release OTLP held 65 records with the 136 drops explicitly retained — queue-full loss is counted, not presented as exactly-once logging.

Allocated a deliberately imbalanced 75-trial diagnostic plan (10+11+12+13+14+15 across six configurations) that reconciles exactly and yielded 55 validation successes and 20 failures; 55/75 is a mixed number and cannot rank the configurations, the fair comparison uses only the common T1–T10 first seed (60 runs), and no significance conclusion is asserted.

Kept the historical DeepSeek live pilot (72 live runs = 6 configurations × 12 tasks, with 51 validation successes) separate from this refresh, whose 75 diagnostic trials used scripted completions and consumed no new paid API calls; the refresh also passed 330 offline tests with 3 container items skipped rather than counted as passes, and reported 22 runtime cases separately.
limits: The 55/75 pooled count is not a single-configuration success rate: the plan intentionally gives different tasks and repeat seeds to different configurations, so configurations cannot be ranked from it.
75 is not 72 plus 3 failure retries — the allocation table's omissions and additions reconcile to 75 directly, and repeats are pre-arranged independent seed runs.
The fair comparison uses the common T1–T10 first seed (60 runs); it is descriptive and this card asserts no significance conclusion.

0.347 ms is event-loop responsiveness under a fixed 45 ms injected export delay in a local fixture, measured as 10 ms timer wake minus scheduled time; model latency is excluded and it is not a model or total-task speedup.

The two telemetry experiments must stay separate: 24/24 local and OTLP delivery belongs to the limited-latency experiment, while the dedicated blocking experiment ends at 65/201 with 136 drops explicitly retained.
Queue-full behavior intentionally drops and counts spans because the two sinks are isolated best-effort queues; the design does not provide exactly-once logging or a hard shutdown deadline.

The refresh's 75 trials are scripted simulated completions with no new paid calls; only the historical DeepSeek pilot is live, and the three streaming adapters were not all exercised with paid calls in this round.

3 skipped container items are not passes, and 330 offline plus 22 runtime results are separate denominators; the environment is a local 8-core/16 GiB rootless Docker lab with 12 synthetic repair tasks, with no production or cloud evidence.
